summary: Session 12 safety automation. Backend: wrote tests/test_babybabel_session12_safety.py (15 tests, localhost:8001, -n 0). 13/15 pass: the 3-distinct-blocker auto-pause works (2 blocks = still active, same blocker twice = 409, 3rd block = paused). Paused accounts get 423 on /auth/me, other authenticated routes and login (a wrong password still gets 401). They are hidden from /tutors, /tutors?q=, /tutors/map and /tutors/{id}. Admin /admin/suspended shows blocked_by=3. Reinstate restores access, is admin-only and returns 404 when repeated. After reinstatement it takes 3 NEW blockers to pause again (the 4th and 5th blocks don't). Admins can't be blocked. The safety-email GET/PUT is admin-only, returns 422 for invalid input, persists and lower-cases. A safety-reason block sends one email (202); non-safety blocks send none. A block survives account deletion and re-attaches on re-signup with +alias and different case (status true, messaging 403). 2 FAILURES: (a) block evasion with a second alias moves the block off the first alias account; (b) a paused user can't DELETE /auth/me (423), so the 'deleted paused account stays paused' path can't be reached through the API. I checked that branch with a direct DB tombstone: signup returns 423, the user doc is created paused and login returns 423, but no tutor profile is created. Regression: session11 blocks, session10 privacy/spam and blog all pass (43/43). The one CORS failure was caused by my env override and passes when re-run with the public origin. Frontend: Admin Safety panel works (input, Save disabled until changed, success toast, paused rows, Reinstate removes the row + toast). Logging in as a paused user goes to /suspended. A cold start with a paused token goes to /suspended and clears the token. Contact support goes to /support and Back to start goes to /onboarding. FAILURE: a user who is signed in when their account gets paused is signed out but sent to /onboarding, not /suspended (reproduced twice).

critical.issue: Block-evasion hole. When an account is re-created, blocks are re-attached with update_many({blocked_email_fp: fp}) -> set blocked_id=new uid, but blocked_email_fp is kept. Blocked user X deletes, signs up as x+a@ (blocked, correct), then signs up x+b@: all blocks MOVE to x+b and x+a is no longer blocked (status false, can message the tutor). Test: TestEvasion::test_second_alias_does_not_unblock_first. Fix: on re-attach, insert a copy of the block for the new uid (or unset the fp and keep one block per account). Better still, also apply blocks by fingerprint to any live account with the same fp.

minor.issue: Paused users get 423 from current_user, so they can't delete their account. This makes the tombstone 'suspended' branch in delete_account/signup dead code via the API, and blocks a GDPR-style right to erasure. Either allow delete for paused users (a dependency that skips the suspended check) or document it. Test: TestEvasion::test_paused_user_delete_then_resignup_423.

Blocks only carry over through the email fingerprint after deletion. A blocked user who does NOT delete can sign up at once with x+1@ (or gmail dot variants, which aren't normalised) and is not blocked. Consider checking blocked_email_fp / the fingerprint of live blocked accounts at signup.
A re-created paused tutor account gets 423 before the tutor profile is inserted. If the admin later reinstates it, the tutor has no tutors doc (/tutors/me/profile likely 404s).

A 429 'rate_limited' from the email proxy is only logged. The 2 pause alerts at 01:07 were dropped with no retry or queue. For child-safety alerts, add a retry/backoff or persist failed alerts (also show them in the Admin Safety panel).
blocked_by counts all-time distinct blockers, not blockers since reinstated_at. After one reinstatement a re-paused user shows e.g. 6, while suspended_reason says 3. Cosmetic.

ui_bugs.issue: An invalid email shows the toast 'Couldn't save / Request failed' instead of 'Enter a valid email address'. The 422 detail is a pydantic array, so apiFetch throws 'Request failed' and e.message.includes('email') is false. Add client-side email validation, or map 422 to the friendly text. Reference: /app/frontend/src/AdminSafetyPanel.tsx:38

integration_issues.issue: After the 3rd block, tapping the Bookings tab -> /bookings/me returns 423. The token is removed, but the app lands on /onboarding, not /suspended (reproduced twice). RCA: in the auth.tsx onAccountSuspended handler (lines 39-43), setUser(null) and router.replace('/suspended') run together. Then the AuthGate effect in _layout.tsx:30-31 runs with the stale segments[0]==='(tabs)' and user null, so its router.replace('/onboarding') overrides /suspended. Login and cold start work because the user is already null or on an auth route. Fix: keep a `suspended` flag in AuthProvider and have AuthGate route to /suspended (skipping the onboarding redirect) when it is set. Or defer setUser(null) until after the navigation.

action_items: HIGH: Fix the mid-session pause redirect race (auth.tsx onAccountSuspended vs the AuthGate onboarding redirect in _layout.tsx) so the user lands on /suspended.

HIGH: Fix the alias block-evasion hole in signup re-attach. Don't move blocks off an existing live account. Duplicate them per account, or unset blocked_email_fp after re-attach and handle multiple live accounts with the same fingerprint.
MEDIUM: Let paused users delete their account (or decide and document otherwise). The tombstone suspended path can't be reached right now.
MEDIUM: Retry or persist safety alert emails that fail with 429 or a network error.
LOW: Map the AdminSafetyPanel 422 error to the friendly 'Enter a valid email address' message (or add client validation).
LOW: Create the tutors doc for re-created paused tutors (or on reinstatement). Count blocked_by in /admin/suspended since reinstated_at.
critical_code_review_comments: email_fingerprint only strips +tags; gmail dots and googlemail.com are not normalised.
Tombstones are never removed and are updated to suspended=False when a reinstated, re-created user deletes again. That's fine, but tombstones from test runs build up (harmless; test emails only).
optional_user returns None for paused users, so paused tokens act anonymous on public routes. That's intended.
server.py is 1900 lines, well over the 700-line guideline. Consider moving auth/account routes into routes/auth.py.

success_rate.frontend: 86% (6/7 flows: admin panel load, save-disabled state, save + toast, reinstate removes row, paused login -> /suspended, suspended buttons; FAILED: mid-session pause redirect)

seed_data_creation: All data was TEST_ users on @example.com and was cleaned up. pytest reinstated and deleted its users. cleanup_session12_safety_ui.py reinstated and deleted the 15 UI seed users by id/token; /admin/suspended is empty afterwards. The alert email was restored to copperstone17@gmail.com (checked). NOTE: the pytest run sent 4 alert emails to delivered@resend.dev. The UI seed pauses ran after pytest had restored the setting, so 4 'account paused' alert emails about TEST_ users went to copperstone17@gmail.com (2 more were dropped by the proxy's 429). One TEST_ tombstone was inserted directly into account_tombstones and then removed. Seeded accounts were not changed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run the pytest suite with EXPO_BACKEND_URL=http://localhost:8001 -n 0. Helpers send a random X-Forwarded-For so signup/login rate limits don't trigger when hitting the backend directly. When running session10 CORS tests, don't override EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL with localhost. To test the mid-session pause in the UI: run tests/seed_session12_safety_ui.py (prints P=paused and Q=2 blocks plus blocker tokens), log in as Q, POST /api/blocks with blockers[2] via page.request, then tap the Bookings tab. Set the alert email to delivered@resend.dev BEFORE seeding so the owner isn't emailed. Clean up with cleanup_session12_safety_ui.py <seed json files>.
rca_of_issue: Mid-session redirect: React batches setUser(null) and router.replace('/suspended'). The AuthGate useEffect then runs with segments still at (tabs) and user=null and calls router.replace('/onboarding'), which wins. Alias evasion: signup's update_many re-points every fingerprinted block to the newest account and keeps blocked_email_fp, so each new alias signup steals the blocks from the previous alias.
